findings.failure_path: When python3 is missing or the helper is unreadable, a Claude Edit/Write/NotebookEdit on a protected primary checkout now only gets a systemMessage and is allowed. The previous jq-only path extraction enforced the deny, so this is a new silent isolation bypass on hosts without python3.
findings.smallest_fix: When the tool is not apply_patch, fall back to the previous jq extraction of file_path/notebook_path/path and run check_target instead of exiting.

findings.failure_path: The loop prints and exits on the first non-empty per-target response. If an early target yields an ask, which apply_patch converts to advisory additionalContext, a later target that would be denied is never checked, so the patch proceeds.
findings.smallest_fix: Check every target first. Emit any deny if one exists, and fall back to the first advisory only when no target is denied. Add a test with an advisory target followed by a deny target.

findings.failure_path: Acceptance and evidence cover target-goal grants (repository, numeric target, expiry, one use, revocation), Codex doctor inventory and session-policy packaging. The implementing files (guard-merge-authorization.sh, merge-authorization-prompt.sh, codex-hooks.ts, operations.ts, package.json, install scripts) are listed in the changes but missing from the review packet, so the merge-authorization boundary cannot be verified.
findings.smallest_fix: Re-run the review with a packet that includes the merge-authorization hooks and tests and the package/installer diffs before claiming release readiness.

concern_results.conclusion: Patch target parsing and the Stop formatter follow their tests. Owner-dispatch stops checking a multi-target apply_patch at the first non-empty response, so an advisory result can hide a later deny. The target-goal grant and doctor inventory changes are not in the packet, so those acceptance items cannot be verified.

Patch text is never executed and a malformed patch is denied. If python3 is missing, Claude Edit/Write isolation and the Claude delegation ask now degrade to allow, where they were previously enforced with jq alone.

FIFO transcripts, oversized input and malformed JSON fail soft with static messages. Once the extraction Stop hook blocks, stop_hook_active is true and the proposed-next hook stays silent. That ordering interaction is minor.
The host-input and proposed-next tests cover deny, allow and degraded paths. No test covers a missing python3 with non-patch Claude edits, or an advisory first target followed by a deny target.
Codex output avoids permissionDecision ask. The new python3 dependency on the Claude Edit path is a compatibility regression.

Packaging for session-policy.md and host-input.py in the npm/OpenCode package is not in the packet (package.json, operations.ts and the install scripts are listed but not shown). The claim that installed paths resolve cannot be verified.
Degradation messages are bounded and do not echo payloads. This is adequate.

The plan and self-review claim target-goal grant semantics and doctor inventory, but the implementing diffs (guard-merge-authorization.sh, merge-authorization-prompt.sh, codex-hooks.ts) are absent from this packet. Those claims are unsupported here.
The merge-authorization boundary change (repository binding, expiry, one use, revocation) is not in the packet and cannot be reviewed. This is a material evidence gap.
hooks/AGENTS.md requires fail-closed behavior where safety requires it. The python3 degradation on the Claude edit path conflicts with that rule, and the diff does not declare the deviation.
